question: Create a concept interior model of the real Helsinki Central Library Oodi, focusing on the top-floor Book Heaven reading room with the Citizens' Balcony, curved wood volume, wave ceiling, glass facade, and double-helix stair.

target.scope: Top floor Book Heaven / Citizens' Balcony interior concept

channels.agent_reach: unavailable in this environment; Codex web research used as the research channel

sources.title: Helsinki Central Library Oodi - ALA Architects
evidence: The design is organized around three individual floors.
The top floor is a calm, contemplative library space with city and park views.
An arching wooden volume creates the contrast and vertical connections between the open floors.
The official gallery identifies top-floor views, the double-helix stair, balcony, and sections.
Program includes library functions, group work, studios, maker space, cafe, restaurant, cinema and event spaces.

sources.title: The floors of Oodi - Oodi Helsinki Central Library
evidence: The third floor is Book Heaven, Citizens' Balcony and children's section.
The top floor is for relaxing and unwinding under an undulating ceiling.
The top floor includes a cafe, seven reading oases, 100,000 books and a children's section.

sources.title: Helsinki Central Library Oodi - European Commission Culture and Creativity
evidence: The layout divides functions into a lively ground floor, a peaceful upper floor and an enclosed in-between volume.
The glass facade extends the public square into the ground floor.
The third floor preserves the traditional library atmosphere and features the Citizens' Balcony.
The middle floor sits inside a curved wooden mass that connects the levels.

sources.title: Oodi Helsinki Central Library / ALA Architects - ArchDaily
evidence: Materials are identified as wood, glass and concrete.
The project gallery and floor-plan references support a large open reading floor and balcony relationship.

research_limits: No public measurement set for the selected camera area was found.
The model is a spatial concept, not an exact survey or construction document.
Furniture positions, dimensions and ceiling wave amplitude are inferred for visual completeness.
